versions.summary: Install the skill as a plugin in Claude Code, Codex or Copilot CLI, or with npx skills in most other agents. Agents that can't publish to claude.ai now always make the single-file version.

entries.text: Install it as a plugin in Claude Code, Codex or Copilot CLI, with `npx skills` in most other agents, or from a clone with `scripts/install`.
The skill moved to `skills/interactive-questionnaire/`. If you linked the whole clone into `~/.claude/skills`, remove that link and reinstall with one of the methods in the README.
Agents that can't publish to claude.ai now always make the file version, even when you bring the questions ready-made, and open the preview in your browser when they have no built-in one.

versions.summary: The skill can now make a questionnaire as a single HTML file for people who don't use claude.ai: it opens in any browser, travels from person to person with everyone's answers inside, and Claude reads the answers back from a returned copy.

entries.text: A file version for people who don't use claude.ai: `build.py --standalone` writes one HTML file that opens in any browser with no account or server. Each person answers, then «Save a copy with the answers» downloads the file with their answers and everyone's before them, to pass on; whoever collects adds the copies or codes that come back, and `import_answers.py` reads answers straight out of a returned copy. Where a viewer doesn't run the page (a file preview or an attachment preview), the file shows its title and asks to be opened in a browser instead of an empty frame.

versions.summary: Everyone who opens a shared questionnaire now sees the team's answers, and people the page can't save for, including visitors without a Claude account, send theirs as one compressed line that chats can't break.

entries.text: Anyone the page can't save for, including visitors without a Claude account, can send their answers with «Send your answers», which makes a one-line code to paste into a message; the owner pastes it into «Add answers from a code» and the answers join the team's under the sender's name. The code is letters and digits only, with a checksum, so it survives the formatting chat apps and mail clients apply, and a damaged code is refused rather than read wrong.
A config's `legacyLocalKey` brings in answers an earlier version of the page kept in someone's browser, and people who can now save carry those answers into the page.

`scripts/import_answers.py` decodes answer codes, from one person or from «Copy all answers», into documents for the report or for an ArtifactData batch, and `summarize.py` names their senders and takes more than one `--docs` folder.
The skill's sharing advice now says who can save at each share level: on a personal plan, invite teammates by email as Editors with no public link, or keep the link and collect answers by message.

«Copy all answers» now copies everyone's answers, with names, as one compressed line of letters and digits instead of readable text, so chats and email can't reformat it; the owner can paste it back into the page, which adds anyone missing and leaves the rest as they are, or paste it to Claude.
People who open a shared questionnaire without an identity on the page, such as teammates outside your organization, now see the team's answers instead of an empty page.

versions.summary: First public release: a skill that turns your questions into a claude.ai page a team fills in one after another, keeping every answer for Claude to read back.

entries.text: Build a shareable questionnaire page on claude.ai from a JSON config: each person's answers are saved under their name, everyone sees the team's answers, and Claude reads them back into a report.
Three kinds of question: decisions with a recommended answer (yes, a different answer, not sure), multiple choice with your own options, and open questions with a written answer.
Pages in one or more languages, with a switch at the top. Italian and English are built in, and any other language can bring its own wording.

Answering closes the question and scrolls to the next unanswered one. Floating buttons go to the top, the next unanswered question and the last one, and a sidebar lists every question with a tick for your answers (a drawer on phones).

Scripts: `build.py` checks a config and explains every error before building the page, `extract_config.py` gets the config back out of a published page, and `summarize.py` turns the saved answers into a Markdown report.
